title: Make Your Own

content.title: Your project. Your rules.
content.body:
You've built three projects. Now it's your turn to invent one.

It can be a game, a story, a quiz, a simulator, a shop, a sports tracker, a robot helper — anything. There's no single right answer here. You're the one in charge.

The only things your project needs:
• A beginning (greet the player or set the scene)
• At least one place where the player types something with input()
• At least one function you wrote yourself with def
• An ending (tell the player how it went)

content.title: Stuck for ideas?
content.body:
• A treasure hunt where the player picks rooms to search
• A snack vending machine that takes orders and gives change
• A daily mood tracker that asks how you feel and writes a tiny message back
• A 'what should I draw?' generator that suggests random subjects
• A trivia gauntlet that gets harder each round
• A choose-your-own-restaurant that asks what you want to eat
• Remix one of your earlier projects — but bigger, weirder, or funnier

content.title: Plan before you code
content.body:
Before you start typing, take 30 seconds:

1. What's it called?
2. What does the player do?
3. What's the ending?

If you can answer those three, you have a plan. Now build the smallest version of it. You can always make it bigger.

starterCode:
# 🚀 Make Your Own
# Anything goes. Start by saying hi to your player.
progressiveHints: Start small. What's the simplest version of your idea? Build that first — then add to it.
Use `def` to wrap one piece of your project in a function, like `def show_menu():` or `def greet_player():`. Functions keep things tidy.

milestones.label: Asks the player something with input()
Defines your own function with def
Uses if to make a decision

remixIdeas: Add a second function — maybe one for the intro and one for the ending.
Add a score, a stat, or a counter that changes during the game.
Use a loop so the player can do something more than once.
Add a twist — a secret answer, a hidden ending, or a surprise message.
Show your project to someone and ask what they'd add.
